_doc: The Gradient panel menu's three stop transforms (transcripts/GRADIENT.md, Panel menu): Reverse Gradient, Distribute Stops Evenly, Reset Midpoints.
Each vector names an op (reverse | distribute | reset_midpoints) and the stops it takes; expected is the stops list the op returns, or null (refused, nothing written).

reverse: stops in location order (stable), then reversed; each location becomes 100 - location; the midpoint between new neighbours j and j+1 is 100 minus the old midpoint of that same pair; the last stop's midpoint_to_next is 50.
distribute: stops in location order (stable); stop i of n takes location 100 * i / (n - 1) in binary64; every midpoint_to_next is 50.
reset_midpoints: every midpoint_to_next is 50; stored order and locations are unchanged.
All three refuse a value that is not a list, a list of fewer than two stops, or a stop with no numeric location.
Every expected value was computed by hand from the spec text before the law existed; each _comment shows the arithmetic.

vectors.name: reverse_two_stops
vectors._comment: Locations 0, 100 become 100, 0, so blue leads. The one pair's midpoint was 40 from red; from blue it is 100 - 40 = 60. The new last stop (red) takes 50.

vectors.name: reverse_three_asymmetric
vectors._comment: A 0 (mid 30), B 25 (mid 70), C 100. Reversed: C 100 -> 0, B 25 -> 75, A 0 -> 100. Pair C-B was old B-C, mid 70 -> 30. Pair B-A was old A-B, mid 30 -> 70. A is last: 50.

vectors.name: reverse_unsorted_stored_order
vectors._comment: The same three stops stored C, A, B. In location order they are A, B, C, so the answer is reverse_three_asymmetric's. A law that reverses STORED order would return B, A, C with locations 75, 100, 0.

vectors.name: reverse_missing_midpoint_reads_50
vectors._comment: The first stop has no midpoint_to_next; it reads as 50 (gradient_host::stops_from_json), so the reversed pair's midpoint is 100 - 50 = 50.

vectors.name: reverse_tie_keeps_stored_order_then_flips
vectors._comment: A 0 (mid 10), B 50 (mid 20), C 50 (mid 30), D 100, stored B before C. Location order is stable, so A, B, C, D; reversed D, C, B, A at 0, 50, 50, 100. Pair D-C was old C-D: 100 - 30 = 70. C-B was old B-C: 100 - 20 = 80. B-A was old A-B: 100 - 10 = 90. A is last: 50. An unstable tie gives D, B, C, A.

vectors.name: reverse_refuses_not_a_list
vectors._comment: A string is not a stops list: refused.

vectors.name: reverse_refuses_stop_without_location
vectors._comment: The second stop's location is missing: refused, not read as 0.

vectors.name: distribute_unsorted_stored_order
vectors._comment: Stored at 100, 0, 30. In location order: 0 (black), 30 (red), 100 (white); n = 3 gives 0, 50, 100, returned in that order.

vectors.name: distribute_two_stops
vectors._comment: n = 2: 0 and 100. The menu row is disabled at two stops; the law still answers.

vectors.name: distribute_tie_keeps_stored_order
vectors._comment: Black 0, red 50, green 50, stored red before green. Stable location order is black, red, green; n = 3 gives 0, 50, 100, so red takes 50 and green 100. An unstable tie swaps them.

vectors.name: distribute_refuses_one_stop
vectors._comment: Fewer than two stops: refused (n - 1 would be 0).

vectors.name: distribute_refuses_stop_without_opacity
vectors._comment: The first stop has no opacity: refused, because the ports' stop parsers refuse it (a stop is colour, opacity, location).

vectors.name: reset_keeps_stored_order
vectors._comment: Stored at 100, 0: the order is kept (no sort), only the midpoints change (40 and 70 become 50).

vectors.name: reset_refuses_not_a_list
vectors._comment: A number is not a stops list: refused.
